implementation: Analyze canonical IR once for all closed-program array aliases, initializers, global rebindings and writes
Invalidate the full alias group for parameters, escaped arrays, unknown definitions, calls and unbounded writes
Use only local array facts in reloadable programs and feed the same immutable ranges to every emission entry
Promote inlined results and simplify correlated success edges before strip mining creates loop-carried initial values
Prove all signed-add/subtract reduction prefixes fit int64 from initial, term and maximum trip-count ranges using i128
Require the continuing loop edge to dominate each proven update and retain checks whenever the proof is incomplete
Run existing field folding and exact reductions before the new CFG simplifications, retaining both early and late consumers
Allow LLVM to vectorize the proven calls and arithmetic loops while preserving normal failure and polling contracts

measurement.aggregation: Median and sample CV from all nine samples; no outlier filtering or wrapper subtraction

semantic_coverage: Global initializers, cross-function writes, rebindings and aliases; escaped values and reloadable globals invalidate the proof
Bounded and unknown trip counts, mixed-sign terms, initial values and both checked add/subtract operations
Updates before the loop condition retain their overflow checks
Standalone AOT calls across zero, one, 1000, 1024, 1025 and 4097 elements with varied signed seeds
Unknown global writes retain leaf overflow, accumulation overflow and exact out-of-bounds prefixes under GC
Existing extreme integer reductions, field aliases, catch/finally, logical traces, stack limits and clean frame ownership

limitations: This is a focused five-pair AOT/C++ comparison, not a new full benchmark-suite average
All measurements retain the real entry and checked-language semantics; no sample filtering or wrapper subtraction
Global range proofs require a closed program and no escaping or unknown writes; unproven arithmetic retains checks
